zh: 表格到处都是,五个不同的登录账号,数据散落在彼此根本不互通的实体之间。

en: We don't assume, oh, we're public radio, so we should be a little bit boring.
zh: 我们不会假设,哦,我们是公共广播电台,所以我们应该有点无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's KCRW.
zh: 这是 KCRW。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, indeed, it's KCRW.
zh: 是的,没错,这是 KCRW。

en: There's like the broccoli and the chocolate cake.
zh: 就像是西兰花和巧克力蛋糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: We try to lean to the chocolate cake.
zh: 我们尽量偏向巧克力蛋糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and sometimes you're broccoli just with a really nice cheese on top or something like that, right?
zh: 嗯,有时候你就是西兰花,只不过上面撒了一层特别好的奶酪之类的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的,完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: KCRW.
zh: KCRW。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder of KCRW, she was a person who really didn't care what other people thought of her.
zh: KCRW 的创始人,她是一个真的完全不在乎别人怎么看她的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a superpower in making decisions.
zh: 这是做决策时的一种超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We fought all the time.
zh: 我们经常吵架。

speaker: Unknown
en: I realized later that was her love language.
zh: 我后来才意识到,那是她表达爱的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would leave every day and go, oh, I'm going to get fired, you know.
zh: 我每天下班离开时都会想,哦,我要被开除了,你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is KCRW.
zh: 这是 KCRW。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally every other aspect of media is controlled by the new kind of almost oligarchs of the world.
zh: 媒体的其他所有方面,几乎都已经被世界上新型的、近乎寡头的人所控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not here to make money, to sell your data, to get you to buy something.
zh: 我们在这里不是为了赚钱,不是为了卖你的数据,不是为了让你买东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just giving you information and trying to make your life better.
zh: 我们只是给你提供信息,并努力让你的生活变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey folks, Jeff Berman here.
zh: 嘿,各位,我是 Jeff Berman。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we start the show, I'm thrilled to welcome my friend, Jamie Batmer, Chief Investment Officer of Creative Planning, one of the sponsors of our show.
zh: 在节目开始之前,我很高兴欢迎我的朋友,Jamie Batmer,Creative Planning 的首席投资官,也是我们节目的赞助商之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative Planning is one of the country's largest independent wealth management firms where a single team, advisors, tax specialists, estate planners, all work from one coordinated plan.
zh: Creative Planning 是全美最大的独立财富管理公司之一,在该公司,一个单一的团队——顾问、税务专家、遗产规划师——全都基于同一个协调的计划开展工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jamie, welcome to the show.
zh: Jamie,欢迎来到节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, thank you so much for having me.
zh: 嘿,非常感谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jamie, when you meet a new client, founder, a business owner, what does their advisor setup usually look like?
zh: Jamie,当你接触一位新客户,一位创始人、一位企业主时,他们的顾问配置通常是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a few investment people, right?
zh: 可能有几个投资方面的人,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: They have it spread out with a few firms.
zh: 他们把资产分散在几家机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they have, you know, a tax person they've been working with or a tax team.
zh: 然后他们有,你知道的,一个一直在合作的税务人员,或者一个税务团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then an estate planning team they've been working with.
zh: 还有一个一直在合作的遗产规划团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we've done is, you know, bring those all under one roof with the dedicated subject matter experts within each space.
zh: 所以我们所做的,你知道的,就是把这些都放到一个屋檐下,在每个领域都有专门的 subject matter 专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to imagine that there's also a set of hidden costs when you have advisors who don't really talk to each other.
zh: 我可以想象,当你的顾问们彼此不真正沟通时,还存在一系列隐性成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do those costs look like that people may not even recognize?
zh: 这些人们可能甚至没有意识到的成本是什么样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's just friction costs.
zh: 这就是摩擦成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not moving along as efficiently as you can be.
zh: 你没有以尽可能高的效率前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's not clear communication between those entities, you're missing stuff.
zh: 如果这些主体之间没有清晰的沟通，你就会遗漏一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're missing the closest thing the free money the markets will give you.
zh: 你错过了市场能给你的最接近免费钱的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you to share a real-world example of a client who came to you after fragmented advice and counsel led to a costly mistake?
zh: 能否请您分享一个真实案例，一位客户因为碎片化的建议和顾问意见导致了代价高昂的错误，后来找到你们？

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a family that was domiciled at one point in Delaware, right?
zh: 我们有一个家庭，曾经注册在特拉华州，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Made total sense when it was set up over a decade ago.
zh: 在十多年前设立的时候，那完全说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, as things have changed, they should be farther out west in Nevada.
zh: 现在，随着情况的变化，他们应该迁到更西边的内华达州。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for this particular entity, it was a nearly $70 million mistake.
zh: 而对这一个主体来说，那是一个将近七千万美元的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's the thing is, is that the person that did this for them, they didn't make the wrong decision in real time.
zh: 但问题在于，为他们做这件事的人，在当时的时点并没有做出错误的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: They took care of it and then they left, right?
zh: 他们处理好了然后就离开了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is constantly looking at it.
zh: 关键是要持续不断地审视它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where we can add value.
zh: 这就是我们能创造价值的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: This team is looking to analyze every element of their financial life and make an empirically optimized decision.
zh: 这个团队致力于分析他们财务生活的每一个要素，并做出经过实证优化的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that gives people extraordinary peace of mind that they know they're gonna have individuals that focus on this stuff all day long and not focus on trying to sell people bad stocks.
zh: 这给人们带来极大的安心，因为他们知道会有人整天专注于这些事情，而不是专注于向人们推销糟糕的股票。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your mission?
zh: 你们的使命是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you guys doing this work?
zh: 你们为什么做这份工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Focusing on what we can control, looking at everything, you know, doing it right, not having a conflict of interest in helping people, helping entities, you know, fulfill the dreams they want, you know, give to their family, give the charities.
zh: 专注于我们能控制的事情，审视一切，把事情做对，在没有利益冲突的情况下帮助人们、帮助主体，你知道的，实现他们想要的梦想，回馈家人、回馈慈善机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that's the most fantastic reward you can have.
zh: 我是说，这是你能拥有的最棒的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the why behind it.
zh: 这就是背后的初心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I deeply appreciate how mission-driven you are in that.
zh: 我非常欣赏你们在这一点上的使命驱动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for being with us, Jamie.
zh: 非常感谢你来到我们节目，Jamie。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's such a pleasure to talk with you.
zh: 和你交谈真是非常愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now on to the show.
zh: 现在进入正题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Masters of Scale.
zh: 这是 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Jeff Berman, your host, and I am so excited to be in Los Angeles today with my new friend, Jennifer Farrow.
zh: 我是你的主持人 Jeff Berman，今天我非常激动能和我的新朋友 Jennifer Farrow 一起在洛杉矶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jennifer, I'm thrilled for you to be with us as you've been leading KCRW, a legendary public media institution, through unprecedented, complex times with grace and grit and heart.
zh: Jennifer，你能来到我们节目让我非常兴奋，因为你一直以优雅、坚韧和用心，带领 KCRW——一家传奇的公共媒体机构——走过前所未有的复杂时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have so much to discuss.
zh: 我们有很多要聊的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Masters of Scale.
zh: 欢迎来到 Masters of Scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so happy to be here.
zh: 我非常高兴能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you start your career coming out of college?
zh: 你大学毕业后是如何开始你的职业生涯的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think career is a really big word for what it was.
zh: 嗯，我觉得用「职业生涯」这个词来形容那段经历实在太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I needed a job, so I worked for a criminal defense attorney during the kind of war on drugs and worked as a legal secretary and a paralegal.
zh: 我需要一份工作，所以在那种「毒品战争」时期，我为一位刑事辩护律师工作，担任法律秘书和律师助理。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was it like being a paralegal back in the early 90s in that war on drugs era?
zh: 在九十年代初那个「毒品战争」时代，做律师助理是什么感觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it was a very, you know, big education on the way the world really works, especially for people who don't have money and who were doing what they felt they needed to do to survive and how they were just swept up in a lot of politics.
zh: 我是说，那是一次关于世界真实运作方式的重大教育，尤其是对那些没有钱、做着自己认为为了生存必须做的事的人们，以及他们是如何被卷入大量政治漩涡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you know, and as our regular listeners know, I started my career as a public defender.
zh: 如你所知，也如我们的老听众所知，我是以公设辩护人开始我的职业生涯的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the most valuable lessons for me from my five years doing that work is how to fight when you are radically under-resourced.
zh: 而那段五年工作经历给我最宝贵的教训之一，就是当你在资源极度匮乏时该如何战斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going up against one of the most powerful forces in the world, and you are so radically under-resourced that you just have to be scrappy.
zh: 你要对抗的是世界上最强大的力量之一，而你的资源极度匮乏，你只能拼命想办法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost the best possible training for startup life.
zh: 这几乎是对创业生活最好的训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also you have to get over the fact that things aren't fair, which I think is really important.
zh: 而且你还必须接受事情并不公平这个事实，我认为这一点非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when you're raised a certain way, you look at the world a certain way, you're just like, but wait, that's not fair.
zh: 比如当你以某种方式被抚养长大，你以某种方式看待世界，你就会想：等等，这不公平啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how did you make the jump from a paralegal to a local criminal defense lawyer to KCRW?
zh: 那么你是如何从律师助理、本地刑事辩护律师跳到 KCRW 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the obvious.
zh: 这条路并不显然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would listen to KCRW.
zh: 我当时会听 KCRW。

speaker: Unknown
en: I loved KCRW.
zh: 我热爱 KCRW。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, wow, this is where smart people hang out.
zh: 我当时想，哇，这就是聪明人聚集的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to be where smart people were.
zh: 而我想待在聪明人聚集的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started volunteering at KCRW.
zh: 于是我开始在 KCRW 做志愿者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And KCRW at that time, they're a very robust volunteer program.
zh: 那时候的 KCRW 有一个非常完善的志愿者项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of things, a lot of...
zh: 所以很多事情,很多……

speaker: Unknown
en: Jobs were done by volunteers, really devoted people.
zh: 工作都是由志愿者完成的,那些人非常投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just being around people were so welcoming and kind and really committed to just good things.
zh: 周围的人是那么热情、友善,而且真心致力于做好事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, this is where I want to be.
zh: 我心想,这就是我想待的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just quit and I started volunteering full-time at KCRW.
zh: 我直接辞了职,开始在 KCRW 全职做志愿者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, something will happen.
zh: 我当时想,总会有机会出现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you transition from being a volunteer at KCRW to actually being on staff there?
zh: 你是怎么从 KCRW 的志愿者过渡到真正成为那里的正式员工的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, well, another kind of ridiculous story, but I, so part of my, you know, doing odd jobs to make rent, I got hired by the general manager and the founder of KCRW to transcribe this radio show.
zh: 好吧,又是一个挺离谱的故事,不过,你知道,在我打零工付房租的那段时间里,我被 KCRW 的总经理兼创始人雇去转录一档广播节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for our younger audience, there was no granola back then.
zh: 对于我们年轻的听众来说,那时候还没有 granola(自动转录工具)。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not dealing with AI being able to transcribe in real time.
zh: 我们那时没有 AI 能实时转录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Literally, you are doing the transcription.
zh: 真的,就是你自己在做转录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was manual.
zh: 那是纯手工的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I had used my credit card and bought a laptop on Cash Advance.
zh: 但我用信用卡的预借现金买了一台笔记本电脑。 [[108-118 说明:照原文。]]

speaker: Unknown
en: So this was when Apple laptops were the first Apple laptop.
zh: 那是苹果笔记本电脑,是第一代苹果笔记本电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I went into
zh: 于是当我走进

speaker: Unknown
en: Ruth Seymour's office, the founder, and I shared her this report I did and she saw my laptop and she's like, what is that?
zh: Ruth Seymour 的办公室,就是那位创始人,我把做的报告给她看,她看到我的笔记本电脑,问,那是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, oh, this is a laptop.
zh: 我说,哦,这是一台笔记本电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: She was so impressed with it.
zh: 她对它印象非常深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyway, we talked, I left her office and her assistant walked in and sat down and said, I'm moving to the Peace Corps, I'm going to Cameroon and I'm quitting.
zh: 总之,我们聊了聊,我离开她办公室之后,她的助理走进来坐下说,我要去和平队了,我要去喀麦隆,我要辞职。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so she said, oh my God, I need an assistant.
zh: 于是她说,天哪,我需要一个助理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go get that girl with the laptop.
zh: 去把那个带笔记本电脑的女孩叫回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she sent someone to run down after me and she offered me a job right on the spot to be her assistant.
zh: 所以她派人跑出去追我,当场就给了我一份当她助理的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what did you say?
zh: 那你怎么说的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, at first I said, I don't want to be an assistant.
zh: 嗯,一开始我说,我不想当助理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to be a secretary.
zh: 我不想当秘书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went to college.
zh: 我是上过大学的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I thought, who am I kidding?
zh: 但后来我想,我在骗谁呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no other prospects and I love this place.
zh: 我没有别的出路,而且我热爱这个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I took the job.
zh: 所以我接受了这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How long were you Ruth's assistant?
zh: 你当 Ruth 的助理当了多久?

speaker: Unknown
en: Just two years because I'd had that same thing where I said to her, look, I didn't go to college to be an assistant.
zh: 只有两三年,因为我也遇到过同样的事,我对她说,听着,我上大学不是为了当助理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to go start a career.
zh: 我得去开始一份真正的事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm going to leave.
zh: 所以我要走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she said, well, what if you stayed here?
zh: 然后她说,那如果你留在这里呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you do?
zh: 你会做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, oh, you need a number two because people were really afraid of her.
zh: 我说,哦,你需要一个二把手,因为大家都很怕她。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was not.
zh: 我不怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people would come and talk to me and I would kind of, you know, whisper to her, figure her out.
zh: 所以大家会来跟我聊,我再去跟她小声传话,琢磨她的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she's like, OK, yeah, you can do that.
zh: 她说,行,好,你可以这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a new job in the legacy organization.
zh: 在这样一个老牌机构里,这可是个新岗位。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did it work?
zh: 那是怎么运作的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, what ended up, I mean, all credit to her, RIP, but she not only built this really unusual entity, KCRW, but she also was so
zh: 我的意思是,最后……我意思是,所有功劳都归她,愿她安息,但她不仅建立了这个非常独特的机构 KCRW,而且她还对我如此

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to me.
zh: 欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we fought all the time.
zh: 所以我们经常吵架。

speaker: Unknown
en: I realized later that was her love language.
zh: 我后来才意识到,那是她表达爱的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would leave every day and go, oh, I'm going to get fired.
zh: 我每天下班都会想，哦，我要被开除了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But she liked that because she liked people to tell the truth to her.
zh: 但她喜欢那样，因为她喜欢人们对她说真话。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's so smart, big personality.
zh: 她非常聪明，个性很强。

speaker: Unknown
en: People would cower from her.
zh: 人们在她面前会畏缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was...
zh: 但我……

speaker: Unknown
en: Too young to understand that I should be doing that to keep my job.
zh: 我是一个非常有好奇心的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she would just keep me in on every decision.
zh: 所以她会让我参与每一个决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: She would sit me in her office and tell me these stories.
zh: 她会让我坐在她的办公室里，给我讲这些故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes I'd say like, this is my job is listening to her tell these tales.
zh: 有时我会想，我的工作就是听她讲这些往事。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, what I realize now is, you know, I may not have had that, you know, that phrase, like, you don't have a seat at the table, but you're in the room.
zh: 不过，我现在意识到，你知道，我可能没有那种，你知道，那种说法，就像，你在桌上没有席位，但你在房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in the room for everything.
zh: 每件事我都在房间里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I under, I started to learn how she made decisions and why.
zh: 而且我，我开始了解她是怎么做决定的，以及为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was invaluable.
zh: 那是无价的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How long did you do that?
zh: 你做了多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think 16 years.
zh: 我记得是16年。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a long time.
zh: 那很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: You strike me as someone who doesn't lack for ambition in a good way.
zh: 你给我的印象是一个不缺野心的人，是好的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't say that critically at all.
zh: 我完全不是批评地说这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why was it comfortable doing that job for 16 years?
zh: 为什么那份工作你做16年还觉得很舒服？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's such a unique space.
zh: 这是一个非常独特的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the largest door opener to culture in Los Angeles.
zh: 它是通往洛杉矶文化的最大敲门砖。

speaker: Unknown
en: Music, food, politics, policy.
zh: 音乐、美食、政治、政策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything, if you're interested in anything, KCRW is a door opener for you to learn more about it.
zh: 任何事情，只要你对任何事情感兴趣，KCRW 都是你深入了解它的敲门砖。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm addicted to that.
zh: 所以我对此上瘾了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a really curious person.
zh: 我是一个非常有好奇心的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love to learn things myself personally.
zh: 我个人很喜欢学习东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also, it was a place where I could have a big effect.
zh: 而且我还觉得，这是一个我能产生重大影响的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I felt like I was able to make things happen.
zh: 你知道，我觉得自己能够推动事情发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think KCRW is just so singular.
zh: 我觉得 KCRW 就是如此独特。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big is KCRW now?
zh: KCRW 现在有多大？

speaker: Unknown
en: How many employees do you have?
zh: 你们有多少员工？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have about 140.
zh: 我们大约有140人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What makes KCRW different from other public radio stations?
zh: 是什么让 KCRW 与其他公共广播电台不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you're right.
zh: 因为你说的对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, whether it's going back to Jonathan Gold, the iconic Los Angeles food critic, or it's left, right and center.
zh: 我是说，无论是追溯到 Jonathan Gold，那位标志性的洛杉矶美食评论家，还是 Left, Right and Center 节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, KCRW has made such a mark, not just in LA, but nationally with the programs that it has created and produced and distributed.
zh: 我是说，KCRW 不仅在洛杉矶，在全国都留下了深刻的印记，凭借它所创作、制作和发行的节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think it just comes from this notion that we don't put ourselves in any kind of box.
zh: 你知道，我觉得这源于这样一种观念：我们不把自己放进任何框框里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't assume, oh, we're public radio, so we should be a little bit boring.
zh: 我们不假设，哦，我们是公共广播，所以我们应该有点无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's like a mindset.
zh: 我觉得这更像是一种心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think when a lot of public radio shifted, and I think I'm glad they did, and I'm really supportive of it, but there's this real big focus on journalism with a capital J and being the local news source and kind of replacing the newspaper.
zh: 你知道，我认为当很多公共广播转型的时候，我很高兴他们那么做了，我也非常支持，但那时有一种对大写 J 的新闻业的强烈关注，要做本地新闻来源，某种程度上要取代报纸。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of towns, which again, absolutely valuable and critical.
zh: 在很多城镇，这再一次说，绝对是宝贵且关键的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think what happened in that transition is we forget about all the other parts of the newspaper that people used to read.
zh: 但我认为在那次转型中发生的事情是，我们忘记了报纸上人们过去会读的所有其他部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of them are playing games or reading comics so they could laugh or finding out where movies or which movies to see and where to eat and things like that.
zh: 有些人玩游戏，或者看漫画以便开怀大笑，或者查找该看哪些电影、去哪里吃饭之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the part that KCRW really embraces because we know that people want that.
zh: 那正是 KCRW 真正拥抱的部分，因为我们知道人们想要那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's like the broccoli and the chocolate cake.
zh: 所以就有西兰花和巧克力蛋糕之说。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are like, we try to lean to the chocolate cake.
zh: 我们呢，我们尽量偏向巧克力蛋糕那边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and sometimes you're broccoli just with a really nice cheese on top or something like that, right?
zh: 嗯，有时你是西兰花，只是上面盖了一层很棒的奶酪之类的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 对，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much of this is touch and taste.
zh: 这其中很多都关乎触感和品味。

speaker: Unknown
en: What has made KCRW so good at being successful over and over and over again, particularly across categories, which is extremely rare for a media organization to do?
zh: 是什么让 KCRW 一次次取得成功,尤其是在不同类别之间都能成功,这对一个媒体机构来说是极其罕见的?

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that Ruth Seymour taught me was, you know, she was a person who really didn't care what other people thought of her, which is a very, it's like a superpower.
zh: Ruth Seymour 教给我的是,你知道吗,她是一个非常不在乎别人怎么看她的人,这就像是一种超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also not so great sometimes, but it's a superpower in making decisions.
zh: 有时候也不太好,但在做决策方面这是一种超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it comes to...
zh: 而当涉及到……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, talent and work product or artistic expression, it can be really hard to tell someone this isn't meeting the mark, you know?
zh: 你知道,人才和工作成果或艺术表达时,要告诉别人「这个没达到标准」真的很难,你懂吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think having that feeling and that culture of knowing, like, this is important and you have to make hard decisions sometimes and you have to move on from things that didn't work out and try new things.
zh: 但我认为,拥有那种感觉和那种文化,知道这一点很重要:有时候你必须做出艰难的决定,你必须放下那些没成功的事情,去尝试新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think, you know, it's that kind of dedication to being really honest.
zh: 所以我认为,就是这样一种对真正诚实的执着。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we can all tell ourselves that like, well, the show's interesting because it's about the environment or whatever, but it's really kind of a bore.
zh: 你知道,我们都可以对自己说,这个节目很有意思,因为它是关于环境之类的,但其实挺无聊的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really, it's powerful to be able to say, this is boring.
zh: 能够说出「这很无聊」,这是很有力量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you started at KCRW, radio was radio.
zh: 当你刚开始在 KCRW 工作时,广播就是广播。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the medium of radio has evolved to be radio plus podcasting plus video plus Lord knows what else.
zh: 随着广播这个媒介演变成广播加播客加视频加上帝知道还有什么,

speaker: Unknown
en: How have you adapted and how has KCRW adapted to meet the changing moment?
zh: 你是如何适应的,KCRW 又是如何适应不断变化的时代的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's a big one.
zh: 嗯,这是个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's probably our biggest challenge ever.
zh: 我想说,这可能是我们有史以来最大的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm sure we'll talk a little bit about federal funding and stuff like that, that being a challenge.
zh: 我相信我们会稍微谈到联邦资助之类的事情,那也是一个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the biggest challenge is this audience shift.
zh: 但我认为最大的挑战是受众的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, like you said, when radio was radio, there was a finite number of, you know, stations and possibilities.
zh: 所以,就像你说的,当广播还是广播的时候,电台和可能性是有限的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you wanted to consume media, you had two choices, like five television stations and, you know, in L.A. maybe...
zh: 如果你想消费媒体,你只有两种选择,比如五个电视台,还有,你知道,在洛杉矶大概……

speaker: Unknown
en: 80 radio stations.
zh: 80 个电台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, when you were in the car, that was your only media that was live and available to you and easy to use.
zh: 然后当你坐在车里,那是你唯一能获得的、实时可用且易于使用的媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now it's like, it's really about changing from the focus being on making the media to really building the community.
zh: 所以现在,这真的是关于把焦点从制作媒体转变为真正建设社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for us, because we are supported by members, so we do care about who's in our audience.
zh: 而且我认为对我们来说,因为我们是由会员支持的,所以我们确实在乎我们的受众是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want people who will actually
zh: 我们想要那些真正

speaker: Unknown
en: Love us enough to support us that the focus now is really on what is it that we're doing that can build a community that will stay together and care about you enough to support you when there's so many choices.
zh: 爱我们到愿意支持我们的人,所以现在的焦点真正在于:我们在做的事情中,什么能够建设一个会凝聚在一起、并且在乎你到在这么多选择面前依然支持你的社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so let's go back.
zh: 好,那我们回到过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So 16 years as assistant GM to Ruth, what happens that you take the GM title?
zh: 你做了 16 年 Ruth 的副台长,发生了什么让你拿到了台长的头衔?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Ruth Seymour retired.
zh: 嗯,Ruth Seymour 退休了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was the main thing.
zh: 所以这是最主要的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had to apply and win the job.
zh: 我必须去申请并赢得那份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But she did something really powerful.
zh: 但她做了一件非常有力量的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: She said, I am going to, I'm not going to sit on the board.
zh: 她说,我打算,我不会进入董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to disappear because I want the next person to take over this place and have the same freedom that I had.
zh: 我会消失,因为我希望下一个人接管这个地方时,能拥有和我一样的自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was what she gifted to me.
zh: 那是她给我的礼物。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was fantastic.
zh: 所以那太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of times founders will stay on a board.
zh: 我认为很多时候创始人会留在董事会里。

speaker: Unknown
en: She was like, no, I'm not going to do that.
zh: 她就像,不,我不打算那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she didn't call me.
zh: 而且她没有给我打电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: She just said, if you need me, call me, but I'm not going to call you.
zh: 她只是说,如果你需要我,就打给我,但我不会打给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was a big, huge gift to me.
zh: 这对我来说是一份巨大、巨大的礼物。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the biggest thing that you changed from Ruth's era when you came into the leadership job?
zh: 当你接任领导职务时,相比 Ruth 的时代,你做出的最大改变是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I was going to say I was a lot nicer.
zh: 我本想说我友善多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that may be the answer.
zh: 我的意思是,这也许就是答案。

en: The guests and topics are just as compelling and timely from Ford's CEO to NASA's administrator to the lessons from the Devil Wears Prada.

en: It takes about 10 seconds to find.
zh: 找到它只需要大约 10 秒钟。

en: Just search Rapid Response wherever you listen to podcasts and hit follow to make sure you never miss an episode.

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope to see you there.
zh: 希望在那里见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类的智力永远不会超过 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be two types of companies.
zh: 未来将有两类公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一类是擅长 AI 的,另一类是因为不擅长而倒闭的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为中心的未来?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana Elkayubi, and on my podcast, Pioneers of AI, we answer that question and so many more.
zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 中,我们回答这个问题以及更多其他问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an AI scientist, entrepreneur, and investor, I know what it takes to build AI that works for everyone.
zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、企业家和投资人,我知道打造对每个人都有效的 AI 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week, I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周,我会与塑造我们未来的先驱者们坐下来交谈,带你们深入了解正在改变我们生活的 AI 幕后故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Pioneers of AI wherever you tune in.
zh: 在你收听的任何地方都能找到 Pioneers of AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We live in an era of unprecedented, at least because of the means by which it can be communicated, misinformation and disinformation.
zh: 我们生活在一个虚假信息和恶意信息空前泛滥的时代——至少就其传播手段而言是空前的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're dealing with propaganda spreading at a rate that the world has never seen before.
zh: 我们正在应对以这个世界前所未见的速度传播的宣传内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about KCRW's role in countering that?
zh: 你如何看待 KCRW 在对抗这一现象中的角色?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's really important.
zh: 是的,我认为这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that, you know, so we've talked before about like the change in audience behavior and the fact that people have many other choices and radio is not a growth medium.
zh: 而且我认为,你知道,我们之前聊过听众行为的改变,以及人们有很多其他选择、广播不是一个增长型媒介这个事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very valuable and powerful medium, but it's not where you're going to find or attract your new audience.
zh: 它是一个非常宝贵且强大的媒介,但它不是你能找到或吸引新受众的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that's where KCRW's transition has been the most powerful is really understanding ourselves as this community resource and not just for LA, but for all of the country.
zh: 但我认为 KCRW 的转型最有力的地方,正在于真正把我们自己理解为一种社区资源——不仅是为了洛杉矶,而是为了整个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a, you know, the brand of public radio is one that you know that these are people committed to serving the community.
zh: 而且作为,你知道,公共广播这个品牌让人们知道,这些人是致力于服务社区的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not here to make money, to sell your data, to get you to buy something.
zh: 我们在这里不是为了赚钱、不是出售你的数据、不是让你买什么东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just giving you information and trying to make your life better.
zh: 我们只是给你提供信息,努力让你的生活变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a world that we live in where literally every other aspect of media is controlled by the new kind of almost oligarchs of the world, it's powerful to have that and to know it exists.
zh: 在我们所生活的这个世界里,媒体的其他方方面面几乎都被新式的、几乎算是寡头的人所控制,拥有这样的存在并且知道它存在,是非常有力量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that what we watch is like, you know, listening behavior changing or habits changing.
zh: 我认为我们所关注的是,你知道,收听行为在改变,或者习惯在改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe people aren't with us every single day, but those who know of us know they can completely and implicitly trust us.
zh: 所以也许人们不会每天都和我们在一起,但那些了解我们的人知道,他们可以完全地、不假思索地信任我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having those things in the world is more critical than ever right now because you just don't, where do you turn?
zh: 在当今世界,拥有这样的存在比以往任何时候都更加关键,因为你就是不知道,你该转向哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, whatever channel that you are consuming media on, it can be manipulated or has been manipulated.
zh: 你知道,无论你通过什么渠道消费媒体,它都可能被操纵,或者已经被操纵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having, you know, public media in the country is critical for that, as a backstop, as a place that you can turn to find out what's real.
zh: 拥有,你知道,这个国家的公共媒体对此至关重要,作为一种兜底保障,作为一个你可以转向去弄清什么是真实的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've got this weird paradox where on the one hand you're labeled by some parties as quote unquote state media.
zh: 而且你面临着一个奇怪的悖论:一方面,你被某些方面贴上了所谓的「国家媒体」的标签。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the other hand, you're dealing with a massive federal funding battle, which I have to imagine has impacted you to some extent.
zh: 另一方面,你又在应对一场大规模的联邦资金之争,我想这在某种程度上已经影响到了你们。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you deal with that tension?
zh: 你如何应对这种紧张局面?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I mean, I think the great thing is that we were never state media.
zh: 嗯,我是说,我认为好的一面是,我们从来都不是国家媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when you look at the original Public Broadcasting Act that Johnson passed, this was for the good of the country.
zh: 而且我认为,当你看 Johnson 通过的最初的《公共广播法》时,这是为了国家的利益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the kind of the language that's in there is so powerful when you think about it in today's world that we're in, which is like to elevate voices that aren't heard, to be this resource for the country.
zh: 而且当你把它放到现在我们所处的这个世界来思考,其中的语言是非常有力量的,那就是:让那些没有被听到的声音得到提升,成为这个国家的一种资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a colleague who's no longer in public media, but he used to say, we need a public internet.
zh: 我有一位同事,他已经不在公共媒体行业了,但他过去常说:我们需要一个公共互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's public television, public radio, we need a public internet.
zh: 有公共电视、公共广播,我们需要一个公共互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when he first said it, I was like, what are you talking about?
zh: 他第一次这么说的时候,我心想,你在说什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet is public.
zh: 互联网是公共的啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not public, right?
zh: 但它并不是公共的,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's controlled and owned and manipulated by others.
zh: 它被他人控制、拥有和操纵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think that we need these spaces like public parks and public libraries where they are here for the good of the people.
zh: 我确实认为我们需要这样的空间,就像公园和公共图书馆一样,它们的存在是为了人民的利益。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still have that mentality 100% and we're probably more devoted to that than ever without federal funding.
zh: 我们 100% 仍然保持那种心态，而且没有联邦资金后，我们可能比以往任何时候都更加投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what federal funding did was, you know, it's 5% of our budget.
zh: 而联邦资金的作用是什么，你知道的，它占我们预算的 5%。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like 30% of a place like Marfa Public Radio in Marfa, Texas, which is a tiny community, but the radio signals cover 30,000 square miles and they reach people with literally no media and no cell service.
zh: 而在像德克萨斯州马尔法的 Marfa Public Radio 那样的地方，它占了大约 30%，那是一个很小的社区，但电台信号覆盖 3 万平方英里，触达那些真的没有任何媒体、没有手机信号的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so why not have something that actually serves everyone?
zh: 那么，为什么不做一些真正服务于每个人的东西呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible.
zh: 这太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, we're more devoted, like I said, than ever.
zh: 所以，你知道的，就像我说的，我们比以往任何时候都更投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, there's something freeing about not having the federal funding because
zh: 而且，坦率地说，没有联邦资金反而有一种解脱感，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to be in that conversation anymore, you know, because the charges about public media being liberal, those are really old.
zh: 你不必再卷入那种争论了，你知道的，因为关于公共媒体是自由派的指控，那些都是很老套的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was, you know, it used to be focused on Big Bird, and then it got focused on NPR.
zh: 它曾经聚焦在大鸟身上，后来聚焦到 NPR 身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it really couldn't be more true.
zh: 但这在某种程度上确实再真实不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think, you know, the notion of what liberal is, is ultimately
zh: 我是说，我想，你知道的，自由派这个概念归根结底就是

speaker: Unknown
en: Being open and interested and curious about lots of different ideas, that is the kind of the opposite of the word conservative.
zh: 对各种不同的想法保持开放、感兴趣和好奇，这基本上是「保守派」这个词的反面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's where public media has always been.
zh: 所以我认为公共媒体一直就在那个位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you think about the contributions that it's made to America and society, I mean, I was a kid who grew up on Sesame Street.
zh: 但当你想到它对美国和社会做出的贡献时，我是说，我就是看着《芝麻街》长大的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned all kinds of things before I got to kindergarten.
zh: 我在上幼儿园之前学到了各种各样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How amazing to take a media that could
zh: 一种媒体能够

speaker: Unknown
en: make a, you know, turn children into little monsters, but also can turn children into these completely educated, interested, you know, little beings.
zh: 把孩子变成小怪物，但也能把孩子变成这些完全受过教育、充满兴趣的小生命，这是多么了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's powerful.
zh: 我是说，这很有力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, I think the federal funding thing, it's a relief to be out of the political football and spending time on the Hill and...
zh: 所以，是的，我认为联邦资金这件事，能摆脱政治皮球、不用在国会上花时间、

speaker: Unknown
en: talking to Republicans and saying, you know that we represent your community and your voice gets on this channel and you're talking to your voters.
zh: 不用跟共和党人说「你知道我们代表你的社区，你的声音可以通过这个频道传播，你在和你的选民对话」……

speaker: Unknown
en: And privately, they would say like, oh, I know, it's really important to me.
zh: 私下里，他们会说「哦，我知道，这对我来说真的很重要」。

speaker: Unknown
en: But publicly, they'd tow this line that said we were biased and things like that.
zh: 但公开场合，他们会顺着那条线说我们有偏见之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, this idea that concepts such as inclusivity and kindness and fairness are radical leftist ideas that are being promulgated by this dangerous entity of public media is sort of insane.
zh: 是啊，我是说，把包容、善良、公平这样的概念说成是由公共媒体这个危险实体所宣扬的激进左翼思想，这种说法有点疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are neither liberal nor conservative concepts.
zh: 这些既不是自由派也不是保守派的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are deeply rooted concepts across our society.
zh: 这些是深深植根于我们整个社会的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jen, a few years ago, you took on an additional challenge of chairing the NPR board of directors.
zh: Jen，几年前，你接受了另一个挑战，担任 NPR 董事会的主席。

speaker: Unknown
en: You seem like you have a pretty full plate.
zh: 你看起来日程已经相当满了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you decide to do that?
zh: 你为什么决定这么做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I was on the board for a number of years.
zh: 嗯，我在董事会待了好几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, when you criticize something, you should just run it and do it yourself.
zh: 而且，你知道的，当你批评某个东西时，你就应该自己去运营它、亲自去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, no, anyway, I, you know, it was an opportunity to, I think, build cohesion in our public radio system at a time when we were under huge challenges.
zh: 所以，不，总之，我认为那是一个机会，可以在我们面临巨大挑战的时期，在我们的公共广播系统内部建立凝聚力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's funny, inside our system, we think we're really different.
zh: 你知道的，有趣的是，在我们的系统内部，我们觉得自己非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, we're not, right?
zh: 当然，我们并不是，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: People think NPR, public radio, they're interchangeable terms, KCRW, interchangeable, but yet, individually, it can be like herding cats.
zh: 人们觉得 NPR 和公共广播是可以互换的词，KCRW 也可以互换，但单独来看，管理起来可能就像放猫一样散乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw that what we were approaching was a big leadership change at NPR and increasing Republican attacks against our brand, our industry, everything.
zh: 我看到我们即将迎来 NPR 的一次重大领导层变动，以及针对我们的品牌、我们的行业、一切的共和党攻击在不断加剧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was very interested in trying to build something that could lead, hopefully lead NPR and public radio to a better place.
zh: 所以我非常有兴趣去尝试建立某种能够引领的东西，希望能引领 NPR 和公共广播走向一个更好的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jim, the federal funding cut is one thing, to your point, if it's 5% of your budget and you have a large base and you can probably find a way to make up for that with some pain, but not too much difficulty.
zh: Jim，联邦资金削减是一回事，正如你所说，如果它占你预算的 5%，而你有一个庞大的基础受众群，你可能能想办法弥补，虽然有些痛苦，但不会太困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are Marfa, Texas and you cover 30,000 square miles and it's 30% of your budget, boy, that sounds like a much tougher putt.
zh: 但如果你是德克萨斯州的马尔法，覆盖 3 万平方英里，而这占你预算的 30%，天哪，那听起来就难打得多的一杆球了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What has happened across the member station universe since the federal funding cut?
zh: 自联邦资金削减以来，整个成员电台的世界里发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, what we're seeing happen, first of all, there was a big fundraising effort outside, kind of adjacent to our industry that ended up creating this bridge fund that allowed a lot of stations two years of runway.
zh: 我是说，我们看到的情况，首先，在我们行业之外——算是相邻的领域——出现了一场大规模的筹款行动，最终创建了这座过桥基金，让很多电台获得了两年的缓冲期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was really huge.
zh: 所以那真的非常重大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of big foundations nationally came in to support that.
zh: 而且很多全国性的大型基金会参与进来支持了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we haven't seen the kind of market forces that we would have seen normally by the September of that one year where we lost the funding.
zh: 所以我们还没有看到本该在失去资金的那一年九月出现的那种市场力量的冲击。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we're starting to see is the large stations.
zh: 但我们开始看到的是大型电台的动作。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably like 12 to 15 stations that have budgets that are larger than $15 million.
zh: 大概有 12 到 15 家电台的预算超过 1500 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of very tiny stations.
zh: 还有很多非常小的电台。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the larger ones are looking at regional leadership, stepping into both work with all the other
zh: 但那些较大的电台正在考虑区域领导角色，与所有其他

speaker: Unknown
en: Say stations in their state to figure out how could they provide either backend services or acquisitions or something like that, that allows us to have that same kind of public service coverage across the country, but takes away some of the expenses that maybe they don't have to spend.
zh: 比如它们所在州的电台合作，想办法提供后端服务或采购之类的，这让我们能在全国范围内保持同样的公共服务覆盖，同时省去一些可能不必支出的费用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're starting to see that now.
zh: 所以我们现在开始看到这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what that will look like.
zh: 我不知道那最终会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that I think
zh: 我认为

speaker: Unknown
en: It will happen soon is the notion that, you know, you can work really hard to protect what you used to have.
zh: 很快会发生的事情是这样一个观念，你知道，你可以非常努力地去保护你曾经拥有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you can look at the other big forces that are happening around you and look to say, okay, how can we adapt to those?
zh: 或者你可以看看身边正在发生的其他重大力量，然后说，好，我们该如何适应它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: Jen, let's fast forward a couple of years.
zh: Jen，让我们快进几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had a paradigm shift in federal government and Republicans and Democrats come together and say, you know what, this was a mistake.
zh: 联邦政府发生了范式转变，共和党和民主党走到一起说，你猜怎么着，这是个错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really should be funding public media in the U.S. much more robustly.
zh: 我们真的应该更大力地资助美国的公共媒体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you say yes?
zh: 你会答应吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, yes, I would, even though I have, you know, issues with it.
zh: 我是说，会的，我会答应，尽管我对它有些意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think America deserves to have a source of information and a community resource that is funded and supported for everyone.
zh: 但是是的，我认为美国值得拥有一个信息来源和一个社区资源，它是为所有人资助和支持的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amount of money that public radio and public television got from the federal government was like budget dust.
zh: 公共广播和公共电视从联邦政府拿到的钱简直就是预算尘埃。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was insignificant.
zh: 微不足道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, you know, as a matter of principle, just like we have public libraries and public parks, we should have a public media, a source that you know is not manipulated by AI, is not controlled by some oligarch.
zh: 而且我认为，你知道，从原则上讲，就像我们有公共图书馆和公园一样，我们应该有公共媒体，一个你知道不会被 AI 操纵、不被某个寡头控制的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we deserve that.
zh: 是的，我们值得拥有那样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm adamant and like dog, yes, let's do it, as much as it was a pain in the butt.
zh: 所以我很坚决，就像 dog 一样，是的，干吧，尽管那曾是件极其烦人的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we should give up on that.
zh: 我不认为我们应该放弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one thing that's really interesting is when that rescission effort happened.
zh: 而且我觉得有一点非常有趣，就是那次撤资行动发生的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So remember, this was, you know, this rescission effort for USAID and public radio happened at the same time, and it was supposed to be the canary in the coal mine and the beginning of many, many rescissions to come.
zh: 所以记住，你知道，针对 USAID 和公共广播的撤资行动是同时发生的，它本该是煤矿里的金丝雀，是接下来许许多多撤资行动的开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have not seen any yet.
zh: 我们至今还没看到任何后续。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what was interesting was public television and public radio lobbied so hard with all of our representatives, which include many Republicans,
zh: 但有趣的是，公共电视和公共广播非常努力地对所有我们的代表进行了游说，其中包括许多共和党人，

speaker: Unknown
en: We were almost going to defeat that in the House.
zh: 我们差点就在众议院击败它了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was going to be defeated in the House, but four Democrats did not show up to vote.
zh: 那本来会在众议院被否决，但四位民主党议员没有出现投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when Republicans saw that they weren't going to pass it, they switched sides.
zh: 当共和党人看到它不会通过时，他们改变了立场。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was unprecedented in this environment right now because so many Republicans understood their constituents and they know people are like, I want my kids to see Big Bird.
zh: 这在当前环境下是前所未有的，因为那么多共和党人理解他们的选民，他们知道人们会说，我想让我的孩子看到 Big Bird。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I want my kids to, I want myself, I want to learn things about the world and I want to hear the voices of my community.
zh: 你知道，我想让我的孩子，我想让自己，我想了解世界上的事情，我想听到我社区的声音。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's an opportunity to make something really powerful with this spirit.
zh: 我认为有机会凭借这种精神做出真正强大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I think it's going to happen?
zh: 你觉得这会发生吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do not.
zh: 我不觉得。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Roe versus Wade, you know, that has been—how long has that been overturned?
zh: 我是说，罗诉韦德案，你知道，那个已经被——被推翻多久了？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that hasn't come back, even though a majority of the country actually supports that.
zh: 而且它还没恢复，尽管这个国家的大多数人实际上支持它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, significant majority, super majority of the country.
zh: 是啊，显著的多数，这个国家的绝对多数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, I don't think that Congress can actually do anything like this.
zh: 所以就是这样，我不认为国会实际上能做成这样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not yet.
zh: 现在还不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not yet.
zh: 现在还不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not yet.
zh: 现在还不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'll try.
zh: 但我会尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to keep trying.
zh: 我会继续尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go down the hill.
zh: 下山去吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keep hope alive.
zh: 让希望活下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keep doing it.
zh: 继续做下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jen, I have a 16-year-old who is extremely online.
zh: Jen，我有一个 16 岁的孩子，他极度沉迷网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: And thank goodness he is quite media literate because he'll assert something and I'll ask him his source.
zh: 而且谢天谢地他相当有媒介素养，因为他会断言某件事，而我会问他的信息来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he now knows that TikTok is not a source.
zh: 他现在知道 TikTok 不是信息来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: The account on TikTok might be.
zh: 但 TikTok 上的某个账号可能是。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's KCRW on TikTok, that's one thing.
zh: 如果是 KCRW 在 TikTok 上的账号，那是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we live in this world where the now trillion dollar companies that control these algorithms are incentivized to drive engagement and engagement happens more when we are outraged and we are inflamed and cortisol is spiking.
